summary:
MISSION CONTROL – Bridging Abstract Aerospace Trade-Offs

MISSION CONTROL is an interactive space mission simulation game designed to make aerospace engineering concepts engaging and accessible through gameplay. It allows players to experience the challenges of planning, designing, and managing space missions while making critical engineering decisions.

The game features three distinct mission scenarios: Earth Observation, Lunar Exploration, and Mars Exploration. Players must balance competing mission constraints, including spacecraft mass, power consumption, budget, and delta-v, while using physics-based simulations to understand how their decisions affect mission feasibility and performance.

By integrating interactive gameplay, real-time resource management, and a simulated mission lifecycle from initial planning to orbital operations, MISSION CONTROL transforms complex aerospace trade-offs into an engaging learning experience. It addresses the lack of practical exposure to space mission engineering among students, encouraging strategic thinking, problem-solving, and engineering decision-making while introducing the fundamentals of real-world planetary exploration.

Project Details – MISSION CONTROL: Bridging Abstract Aerospace Trade-Offs

MISSION CONTROL is an interactive space mission game that gives players an opportunity to experience the challenges of planning and managing real-world space missions. Our main idea is to turn complex aerospace engineering concepts into an engaging, hands-on gaming experience where players learn by making decisions and exploring their outcomes.

The game features three different mission scenarios: Earth Observation, Lunar Exploration, and Mars Exploration. Each mission comes with its own objectives and challenges. Players must carefully manage important resources such as spacecraft mass, power consumption, mission budget, and delta-v. These factors directly influence mission feasibility and performance, helping players understand that every decision in space mission planning involves trade-offs.

The main benefit of MISSION CONTROL is that it connects theoretical knowledge with practical learning. Instead of simply reading about space missions, players can experiment with different mission configurations, understand the consequences of their choices, and learn basic principles of orbital mechanics and resource management.

What makes our project creative is its combination of game design, physics-based simulations, and mission engineering. We wanted to make space exploration more interactive and accessible, especially for students who rarely get the opportunity to experience the complete mission lifecycle.

During development, our team considered scientific concepts, resource limitations, mission feasibility, user interaction, and educational value. Our ultimate goal is to inspire curiosity about aerospace engineering and help students develop critical thinking, strategic planning, and problem-solving skills through an enjoyable gaming experience.
